R' Yehuda (bar Ilai) as cited in the baraitot of 12a.13, 13a.11, 13a.18, 14b.12, 15b.14
Ahasuerus, whose words the narrators report
Haman, whose words Rava (13b.16-19) and the stam's narrative (16a.4-10) report
Mordechai, whose words the stam's narrative reports
Queen Esther, whose words R' Levi (15b.7-8) and the stam (16a.17) report
תנו רבנן (15b.12-15): why Esther invited Haman
the tanna R' Elazar of the baraita at 15b.12
Elijah, whom Rabba bar Avuha met (15b.16)
רבי שילא איש כפר תמרתא, whose derasha R' Asi reports (16a.1)
the Rabbis sitting before Mordechai (16a.6-7), in the stam's narrative

props.gloss_en: R' Elazar: she laid traps for him, as said 'let their table become a trap before them' (Ps 69:23)
R' Yehoshua: she learned from her father's house, as said 'if your enemy is hungry, give him bread' (Prov 25:21)
R' Meir: so that he would not take counsel and rebel
R' Yehuda: so that they would not recognise that she was Jewish
R' Nechemya: so that Israel would not say 'we have a sister in the palace' and divert their minds from prayer for mercy
R' Yosei: so that he would be available to her at all times
R' Shimon ben Menasya: [she thought] perhaps the Omnipresent will take note and perform a miracle for us
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: [she thought] I will show him a friendly face so that he and I will both be killed
Rabban Gamliel: he was a fickle king
R' Gamliel: we still need [the reason of] the Modai
a baraita, R' Eliezer HaModai: she made the king jealous of him and the ministers jealous of him
Rabba: 'pride comes before a fall' (Prov 16:18)
Abaye and Rava both said: 'in their heat I will make their feasts' (Jer 51:39)
Rabba bar Avuha found Elijah and asked: according to whom did Esther see fit to act so? -- according to all the tannaim and all the amoraim
and how many were 'the multitude of his sons' (Esth 5:11)? Rav: thirty -- ten died, ten were hanged, ten went begging at doors
the Rabbis: those who went begging were seventy, as written 'the sated (seve'im) hired themselves for bread' (1 Sam 2:5) -- read 'seventy' (shiv'im)
Ramei bar Abba: they were two hundred and eight in all, as said 'and the multitude (verov) of his sons'
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it is written 'verob' [defectively, without the vav]
'on that night the king's sleep was disturbed' (Esth 6:1): R' Tanchum -- the sleep of the King of the world
the Rabbis: the upper beings were disturbed, the lower beings were disturbed
Rava: the sleep of King Ahasuerus himself
Ahasuerus: what is it that Esther invited Haman? perhaps they are plotting to kill me... is there no friend who would tell me? perhaps someone did me a favour and I did not repay him
'and they were being read' (Esth 6:1) teaches that they were read of themselves
the verse: 'and it was found written' (Esth 6:2) -- 'a writing' would be expected
it teaches that Shimshai was erasing and Gabriel writing
R' Asi: R' Sheila of Kfar Tamarta expounded: if a writing below that is to Israel's merit is not erased, a writing above all the more so
'nothing was done for him' (Esth 6:3): Rava -- not because they loved Mordechai but because they hated Haman
'which he had prepared for him' (Esth 6:4) -- a tanna: for himself he prepared it
Haman: which Mordechai? Ahasuerus: 'the Jew'. Haman: there are many Mordechais among the Jews. Ahasuerus: 'who sits at the king's gate' (Esth 6:10)
Haman: one village or one river suffices for him. Ahasuerus: give him that too -- 'let nothing fall of all you have said'
[Haman] went and found him with the Rabbis sitting before him, teaching them the laws of the handful (kemitza)
Mordechai to the Rabbis: this wicked one comes to kill me -- go from before him lest you be burned by his coal

Haman: what are you engaged in? -- when the Temple stood, one who pledged a meal-offering brought a handful of fine flour and it atoned for him. Haman: your handful of flour has come and pushed aside my ten thousand talents of silver
Mordechai: wicked one, a slave who acquired property -- whose is the slave and whose the property?
Haman: rise, wear these garments and ride this horse, for the king wants you. Mordechai: I cannot until I go to the bathhouse and cut my hair, for it is not proper to use the king's garments so
Esther sent and closed all the bathhouses and barbers; he [Haman] took him into the bathhouse, washed him, cut his hair, and sighed
Haman: a man the king valued above all his officers is now made a bath attendant and barber? Mordechai: wicked one, were you not the barber of Kfar Kartzum?
a tanna: Haman was the barber of Kfar Kartzum for twenty-two years

Haman [kicked as Mordechai mounted]: is it not written for you 'when your enemy falls do not rejoice' (Prov 24:17)? Mordechai: that is said of Israel; of you it is written 'and you shall tread upon their high places' (Deut 33:29)
his daughter, standing on the roof, thought the rider was her father; she threw a chamber pot on her father's head, saw it was her father, fell from the roof and died
and this is what is written 'and Mordechai returned to the king's gate' (Esth 6:12): Rav Sheshet -- he returned to his sackcloth and fasting
'mourning' -- over his daughter; 'and with his head covered' -- over what befell him
the verse: 'Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends... and his wise men said to him' (Esth 6:13) -- they are called both friends and wise men
R' Yochanan: whoever says a word of wisdom, even among the nations, is called wise

his wise men: if he is from the other tribes you can prevail over him; from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim or Menashe you cannot -- Judah, 'your hand on your enemies' neck' (Gen 49:8); the others, 'before Ephraim, Benjamin and Menashe stir up Your might' (Ps 80:3)

R' Yehuda bar Ilai expounded: why these two fallings ('you will surely fall', Esth 6:13)? they said to him: this nation is likened to dust and to stars -- when they descend, to the dust; when they rise, to the stars
'and the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried (vayavhilu) [Haman]' (Esth 6:14) teaches that they brought him in haste
Esther to him: this adversary is not worth the king's damage -- he was jealous of Vashti and killed her, and now he is jealous of me and seeks to kill me
the verse: 'and King Ahasuerus said and he said to Queen Esther' (Esth 7:5) -- the doubled 'said' is the object of למה לי
R' Abbahu: at first [he spoke] through an interpreter; once she told him she came of the house of Saul -- at once 'and he said to Queen Esther' [directly]
